beam_energy.quote: could accelerate electrons to energies of 20 GeV, and later up to 50 GeV

summary.plain: SLAC's two-mile-long linear accelerator, which fires electrons (and, in its early years, positrons) down a straight underground tunnel. It has fed three generations of SLAC's experiments: the original fixed-target program, the SLC and PEP-II colliders, and today the LCLS X-ray laser.
summary.technical: The 3.2 km SLAC linear accelerator (operating since 1966), capable of up to 50 GeV for electrons; injector for the Stanford Linear Collider (1989-1998) and the PEP-II B-factory (1999-2008), and today for the LCLS free-electron laser (not modeled in this wave).
